title: Thermal Energy and Specific Heat
seo_title: Specific Heat Worksheets: q = mcΔT, Heat Flow and Calorimetry (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that the transfer of thermal energy when two components of different temperature are combined within a closed system results in a more uniform energy distribution among the components in the system (second law of thermodynamics).
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on thermal energy and specific heat (NGSS HS-PS3-4): heat flow, thermal equilibrium, q = mcΔT, mixing water and calorimetry. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat flows from hot to cold.
key_sub: In a closed system, energy spreads out until the temperatures are equal.
body_html:
How to think about it

Thermal energy flows from hot to cold until temperatures are equal.

  • q = mcΔT (heat = mass × specific heat × temperature change).
  • In a closed system, heat lost by the hot part = heat gained by the cold part. The final temperature is between the starting ones.
  • Low specific heat (metals): big temperature change. High specific heat (water): small change.
Example

Heat to warm 50 g of water by 10 °C (c = 4.18)?

50 × 4.18 × 10

Answer: 2,090 J

Example

100 g at 20 °C + 100 g at 60 °C?

Equal masses: average

Answer: 40 °C

Common mistakes

  • Thinking “cold” flows into warm objects.
  • Taking a simple average when the masses are different.
  • Thinking a high specific heat means fast warming.

faq.q: What is the formula for heat?
faq.a: q = mcΔT: heat equals mass times specific heat times the change in temperature.

faq.q: How do you find the final temperature when mixing water?
faq.a: Heat lost by the hot water equals heat gained by the cold water, so the final temperature is the mass-weighted average.

faq.q: Why does water heat up slowly?
faq.a: Water has a high specific heat (4.18 J/g·°C), so it needs a lot of energy for each degree.
